questions.prompt: [Module 2: Practical Implementation & Production Patterns] What is the exact output of the following list comprehension snippet?
questions.codeSnippet:
matrix = [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
flattened = [val for row in matrix for val in row]
print(flattened)

options.text: TypeError: list indices must be integers

questions.explanation: In nested list comprehensions in Python, outer loops come first from left to right: for row in matrix, then for val in row.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Production Patterns and Resilience in Python

questions.prompt: [Module 2: Practical Implementation & Production Patterns] Identify why the following function mutates state unexpectedly across calls:
questions.codeSnippet:
def append_item(item, target_list=[]):
    target_list.append(item)
    return target_list

a = append_item(1)
b = append_item(2)

options.text: Default arguments are evaluated once at function definition time, sharing the mutable list instance.
Python functions create a global variable when default arguments are used.
append() returns None rather than the updated list.
Integers cannot be appended to untyped lists.

questions.explanation: Python evaluates default parameter expressions once at definition time. Mutable default arguments (like lists or dicts) are shared across all calls.

questions.prompt: [Module 2: Practical Implementation & Production Patterns] You are processing a 10GB log file on an instance with 2GB RAM. Which Python approach avoids memory exhaustion?

options.text: Read the file line-by-line using a generator iterator (with open(...) as f: for line in f:)
Call f.readlines() to parse all lines into memory at once
Convert the file to a JSON object before looping
Use multiprocessing to load the entire file into 8 concurrent arrays

questions.explanation: Iterating over a file object in Python streams line by line as a generator without loading the entire payload into RAM.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Production Patterns and Resilience in Python

questions.prompt: [Module 2: Practical Implementation & Production Patterns] Which of the following statements about Python's Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) and concurrency are correct?

options.text: The GIL allows only one native thread to execute Python bytecode at a time in CPython
multiprocessing bypasses the GIL by creating separate processes with separate memory spaces
I/O bound operations release the GIL while waiting for network or disk operations
threading provides true multi-core parallel CPU execution for math-heavy loops in CPython

questions.explanation: In CPython, GIL prevents multi-threaded CPU parallel execution, but I/O releases the lock, and multiprocessing spawns separate OS processes.

questions.prompt: [Module 2: Practical Implementation & Production Patterns] What does the '__slots__' attribute do when declared on a Python class?

options.text: It restricts valid instance attributes to a fixed set, eliminating __dict__ to optimize memory usage.
It prevents other classes from inheriting from the declared class.
It automatically serializes class instances to JSON format.
It declares private variables accessible only via getter functions.

questions.explanation: Defining __slots__ on a class prevents the creation of the default __dict__ per instance, significantly reducing memory consumption for millions of objects.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Production Patterns and Resilience in Python
